description: 😎 We’re SMILING FACE WITH SUNGLASSES, competing at the Sarawak Space Challenge 2026 (NASA Space Apps). We’ve built many projects together and ship fast. Skills: full-stack, agentic development, ML/deep learning, and product management. Interests: Earth Science, applying AI agents and ML to real-time Earth observation and astrophysics data. Our team is full, but we’re happy to swap ideas or help with ML and agentic tooling. Say hi! 🚀
summary: Students in Sarawak live through floods, haze and peat fires, yet they mostly learn about them from social media. Sarawak Earth Detectives turns those events into detective cases. An AI "client" watches the news and NASA's near-real-time data, and opens a case when an event can be investigated. The student enters a 3D detective office, visits the scene on a 3D model of Sarawak, picks evidence from decades of NASA Earth data, and tests whether the change is real or just one bad year. An AI partner gives hints but never the answer. The student writes the verdict, the system checks it against statistics computed in code, and a case report is produced. The platform does what the challenge asks (select variables, visualise change over time, measure the rate and test its significance) for the audience the challenge names: students. It matters because the people most affected by a changing Earth should be able to check it for themselves.
details:
Sarawak Earth Detectives

What it is
Sarawak Earth Detectives is an interactive web platform. Students act as detectives and investigate real environmental events in Sarawak, such as peat fires, haze, extreme heat and dry spells. Every case asks one question: “Is this getting worse, or was it just one bad year?”

How it works
Students work in a 3D detective office, which also has a 2D version for older devices. Kenyalang, a hornbill AI partner, guides them through seven steps in 15–20 minutes:

  • Pick a case and read the brief
  • Explore 3D terrain overlaid with NASA fire data
  • Choose NASA climate variables and reject misleading ones
  • Chart trends from 1981 to 2026 and test whether they’re statistically significant
  • Write a conclusion, which code grades out of 100

Benefits

  • Students: Learn statistics hands-on with real NASA data.
  • Teachers: Get ready-made cases and automatic grading.
  • Schools: Get new local cases every week, checked by a human before they go live.

Impact
In 2026, haze closed 710 schools in Sarawak. The project aims to turn students’ worry about climate change into scientific skill, and it supports four UN Sustainable Development Goal targets. It hasn’t been tested in real classrooms yet.

What makes it different

  • Code calculates every number. The AI only gives hints and explains results.
  • “Not enough evidence” can earn full marks.
  • Students sign in with a nickname only.
  • It can be adapted to any region NASA satellites cover.
